title: Accounting conservation, amount safety and transaction semantics
purpose: Find reachable cases where accepted transaction or revert semantics create, destroy, misclassify or expose the wrong value. Apply the companion oracle and ownership contract. Own accounting arithmetic and business-effect atomicity; use replay, projections and checker output only as witnesses, without absorbing FSM/cache mechanics, query-plan semantics or integrity-verifier soundness.
invariants: For every successful transaction or revert and every asset/color bucket, the sum of posting debits equals the sum of posting credits exactly. Conservation is established from the accepted posting list with an independent arbitrary-precision oracle, not inferred from equal stored input/output totals produced by the implementation under audit.

Amount conversion and accumulation preserve the exact unsigned 256-bit value. Zero, maximum and overflow boundaries must be rejected or applied according to the documented operation semantics; no parse, protobuf, Numscript, JSON or aggregation boundary may truncate, wrap, change sign, merge colors or cross asset identities.

A successful direct transaction, Numscript-generated transaction or revert produces one coherent business effect: postings, transaction identity and payload, reference ownership, metadata, ledger sequence and affected volumes describe the same operation. A rejected, failed or skipped order exposes none of those success effects, except the explicitly contractual audit/skip/idempotency and sequence bookkeeping recorded for that outcome.

Within a bulk, accounting effects compose in order against the running overlay. An earlier successful order may fund or constrain a later order; rollback of a failed non-skippable bulk and continuation after a skippable failure must preserve exactly the promised prefix/no-prefix semantics without leaking staged volumes, identifiers, references or metadata.

A revert reverses the exact postings and asset/color buckets of its target once, links both transaction states consistently and applies the requested effective-date and force semantics. Missing or inconsistent allocated transaction state must fail loudly rather than synthesize a different accounting operation.

Equivalent direct postings and Numscript execution, including stored-script version resolution, produce equivalent accepted posting effects under the same committed state and policy. Numscript metadata or address resolution must not mutate the accepted caller intent or bypass amount, balance-floor, account-type or atomicity rules.

Authoritative primary projections of transaction state, balances and volumes equal an independent fold of successful committed business effects at the same audit horizon, including create, revert, skip, ledger deletion and zero-volume purge semantics. Replay is a candidate implementation and evidence source, not the independent oracle.

Business-visible derived totals and volume buckets preserve the same accounting quantities at a declared horizon. Eventual readstore/usagestore values require their documented readiness or progress precondition; projection lag, rebuild and query-plan selection are neighboring domains unless the projection is current and contains arithmetically wrong values.
adversarial_questions: For a multi-posting, multi-asset and multi-color transaction, can any debit or credit be omitted, duplicated, assigned to the wrong bucket, or retained after a later posting fails? What independent per-bucket equation proves the answer?

What happens at 0, 1, 2^64 boundaries and 2^256-1 for direct, Numscript, protobuf/JSON and aggregate paths? Can intermediate source output, destination input, signed balance display or bucket accumulation overflow even when the final-looking result appears valid?

For every rejection point before and after posting production, which WriteSet/overlay mutations, transaction IDs, references, metadata and boundaries exist? Does non-skippable rollback remove all staged success effects, and does skippable continuation retain only the explicit skip outcome while later orders see the right running state?

Can duplicate references, repeated reverts, forced debits, self-postings, world-account postings, empty generated postings, account-type violations or metadata-limit failures create a transaction/log whose volumes were not committed, or committed volumes without the matching transaction/log?

Does a revert read and invert the immutable target postings, preserve asset/color, prevent double reversion and use the correct effective timestamp? Can deletion, missing projection state or aliasing change the target between admission, apply, audit capture and replay?

For an equivalent direct posting set and Numscript result, do both paths enforce balance floors, overflow, chart/account types, metadata precedence and bulk ordering identically? Is the oracle independent of the Numscript producer and production apply helpers?

At one pinned audit horizon, do an independent fold, primary transaction/volume projections and complete authoritative reads agree on identities, postings, reversion links, metadata and input/output values? If they disagree, is the root cause accounting production, verifier coverage, replay/restore, temporal projection lag or query selection?

Can zero-volume purge, ephemeral/transient classification, ledger deletion or post-commit usage/index building cause an arithmetically incorrect exposed total after the documented progress barrier? Separate a wrong accounting annotation/value from a stale, missing or uncertified secondary projection.
dynamic_checks_to_consider: Build a small independent arbitrary-precision reference ledger keyed by ledger/account/asset/color. Generate direct creates, equivalent Numscript creates, reverts, skips and mixed bulks; after every accepted outcome compare per-bucket input/output deltas, transaction fingerprints, references, metadata and boundaries. Do not import production posting, replay, aggregation or model helpers into the oracle.

Exercise a boundary matrix containing zero, one, repeated same-cell postings, self-postings, world and forced sources, multiple colors/assets, 2^64-1, 2^64, 2^256-1 and additions that overflow either side. Assert the exact typed outcome and that a rejection leaves no success projection. A parse error or unrelated admission rejection does not prove apply-time overflow safety.

Inject one failure at each reachable transaction phase after at least one staged mutation and run matched non-skippable and reason-authorized skippable bulks, followed by a successful order that observes the overlay. Compare final primary bytes/logical rows, audit/log outcome, allocated identifiers, references and temporary overlay state with an independently constructed expected prefix.

For revert probes, create a non-empty target through the real apply path, snapshot its immutable posting fingerprint, then vary force, effective date, account type, repeated revert, missing/corrupt target state and same-bulk dependencies. Assert exact reversed postings and paired reversion links; a checker mismatch alone does not prove the producer defect.

At a pinned non-empty audit horizon, independently fold accepted serialized business intent plus the committed success/skip outcome into expected transaction and volume state, then compare primary projections and authoritative reads in both directions. Use production replay only as a third comparator so shared producer/replay logic cannot serve as its own proof.

For readstore/usagestore observations, wait on the documented exact progress/readiness barrier, capture that horizon and compare complete keyed results, not totals alone. Repeat across restart/rebuild only to establish an accounting mismatch; route lost progress, stale serving or restore loss to their owning domains.

Record exact SHA, seed, generated operation trace, horizon, selected production branches, expected/actual per-key state, focused test names and any skipped infrastructure. Demonstrate sensitivity by identifying which deliberate accounting mutation makes the oracle fail. This manifest revision does not run these product probes.
